resources.string: Use home DNS for listed domains
Used on any Wi-Fi or wired network
On Android 9, split DNS pauses while Mullvad is off.
Matches %1$s and everything under it, like nas.%1$s
Your router\'s or home DNS server\'s own address, for example 192.168.1.1 (not 172.27.1.1).
If your home DNS can\'t be reached, listed domains fail instead of asking another server. Other domains work as before.
DNS answers do not add local network rules. Use full names, like nas.home; bare names are not expanded.
Android\'s Private DNS and apps with their own secure DNS (for example Chrome) skip split DNS. Turn them off to use it.
The saved split DNS settings are invalid. Edit them to fix this.
Check the domains, home DNS IP and home network.
Fix or remove the domain that is not valid.
Enter the home DNS server\'s IP address, for example 192.168.1.1.
The home network\'s rule doesn\'t include this address. Add the address to that rule first.
